label: H.R. 9129

latest_action.text: Forwarded by Subcommittee to Full Committee by Voice Vote.

selection.reason: Impact scored and summarised by Gemini.

summary: The GUARD Act of 2026 requires national security agencies to evaluate certain humanoid and quadruped robotics communications equipment and services linked to designated countries of concern. If an agency determines that these technologies pose an unacceptable risk to U.S. national security or the safety of U.S. persons, or fails to make a determination within one year, the equipment or services must be added to the Federal Communications Commission's Covered List, subjecting them to existing bans and restrictions.

affected_groups.effect: Entities in China, Cuba, Iran, North Korea, Russia, and Syria that produce humanoid or quadruped robots or associated communications software face potential prohibitions on importing or selling their equipment in the U.S. if placed on the FCC Covered List.
affected_groups.group: Producers and providers of robotics equipment in countries of concern

affected_groups.effect: Agencies must conduct evaluations, submit reports to congressional committees, and review determinations, while the FCC is responsible for updating and maintaining the Covered List based on these findings.
affected_groups.group: National security agencies and the Federal Communications Commission

key_provisions: Requires an appropriate national security agency to evaluate covered robotics communications equipment or services within one year of enactment to determine if they pose an unacceptable risk to U.S. national security or the safety of U.S. persons.
Mandates that any equipment or services found to pose an unacceptable risk be added to the Federal Communications Commission's Covered List within 30 days.

Stipulates that if a national security agency fails to make a required determination within one year, all covered robotics communications equipment and services must automatically be added to the Covered List.
Requires other national security agencies to review any determination that equipment or services do not pose an unacceptable risk within 180 days.

Defines covered robotics communications equipment or services as any humanoid or quadruped robot or control software produced or provided by entities subject to the influence or control of China, Cuba, Iran, North Korea, Russia, or Syria.

Exact details on enforcement mechanisms beyond referencing existing laws governing the FCC Covered List.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The GUARD Act of 2026 requires national security agencies to evaluate certain humanoid and quadruped robotics communications equipment and services linked to designated countries of concern. If an agency determines that these technologies pose an unacceptable risk to U.S. national security or the safety of U.S. persons, or fails to make a determination within one year, the equipment or services must be added to the Federal Communications Commission's Covered List, subjecting them to existing bans and restrictions.
summary_detail.significance: This bill establishes a mandatory review process for specific categories of advanced robotics tied to adversarial nations, integrating them into the existing federal telecommunications restriction framework if national security risks are identified.
